short: Enthroned as a child without the imperial regalia, he later gambled the court's power and lost.
full:
Go-Toba was installed in 1183 at the age of three, while his half-brother Antoku was still in Taira hands in the west along with the sword, mirror and jewel of the imperial regalia. Antoku drowned at Dan-no-ura in 1185 and the sword went down with him, so Go-Toba reigned without it. He abdicated in 1198 and then governed for over two decades as retired emperor, the real authority in Kyoto, patronising poets and compiling the Shin Kokinshū anthology.

His ambition was to recover from the Kamakura shogunate what the court had lost. In 1221 he declared the regent Hōjō Yoshitoki an outlaw and called the warrior houses to arms. Very few came. The rising collapsed inside a month, and Go-Toba was exiled to the Oki Islands, where he died in 1239. The shogunate deposed the sitting emperor, installed its own candidate, and set up a permanent deputy in Kyoto to supervise the court. No emperor challenged it again for a century.
